instruction: Enable Do Not Disturb mode on Ubuntu and also turn off the automatic screen lock.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.capability_extraction: Can toggle GNOME system settings via the notification panel and UI controls
metadata.explanation: Composite task: (1) enable DND (org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners=false), (2) disable automatic screen lock (org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled=false). Both are 'uninterrupted work' settings. Each sub-goal contributes 0.5 to the score. Getter uses gsettings to read both settings; metric awards 0.5 per sub-goal. [Fixed: inlined bash helper to remove nested 'def _run' — validator requires every def in getter files to start with 'get_']

metadata.task_rationale: Chains DND with disabling automatic screen lock — both are 'focus/work session' settings that prevent interruptions. Navigating to each requires UI interaction with the system settings panel.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners via gsettings, which maps correctly to GNOME Do Not Disturb mode (DND enabled = show-banners false).
Getter correctly reads org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled via gsettings, which maps correctly to the automatic screen lock setting (lock disabled = lock-enabled false).
Both instruction sub-goals are fully covered: DND mode (0.5 credit) and screen lock disabled (0.5 credit), with correct partial scoring.
Getter reads system settings directly via gsettings without relying on UI state, so no postconfig is needed and state timing is not an issue.
Initial config resets show-banners=true (DND off), ensuring the initial environment does not pass evaluation (good negative-control resistance).
Substring check 'false' in gsettings output is reliable since gsettings returns plain 'false' or 'true' text.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric ignores the 'expected' parameter and hardcodes the check for 'false'. Consider using expected.get('show_banners_expected') and expected.get('lock_enabled_expected') for flexibility, though the hardcoded value is correct for this task.
